 I understand where your going witht hat, but that slows her down even farther - now shes using a power to reset her ammo instead of a Played card, meaning shes doing no damage that turn to reset. Compare your alternative power with the current one. She can do 6 damage per round by using 4 cards (gun+ 2 copies of the rounds + speed loading). Moreover, in order to do so she is fully commiting her turn to do so (must use her card, power and draw to make the combo work), and needs 4 cards. Instead, with your alternative power she only needs 2 cards and one power (allowing her to play and draw a card per turn).

You second alternative power is pretty much equivalent to "draw 2 cards at the end of your draw phase", which is a bit OP. Compare it to Bunker's classic power.

The power I suggested allows her to get 1 bullet from the discard directly into pla y (hence faster than speed loading), OR play two cards (if they are ammo ones). In either case it speeds her up, but not to a ridiculously fast speed. I think it is better than her current power, but not as OP as your options. Also, it often happens that she runs out of cards. Allowing her to play from discard helps her to (virtually) increase her hand

As for not using a loaded ammo…indeed several times I wish I hadn't loaded it, but I think that it fits the theme perfectly. Imagine her spending time unloading the special bullets? The answer is to have several weapons, and think before loading It makes playing her correctly a more intersting challenge…and makes sense to have a lot of weapons (and not only useful for unload)

 

Expatriette feels a bit weak when compared to other "gadget" heroes (like wrath). However, with the right support (+damage, heroes that allow other heroes to draw cards) she becomes VERY good. Giving her a boost might be nice, but I feel that a power on the lines you suggest would make her too strong

TheJayMann:

Well, thematically, her power more or less requires her to know she is a mechanical golem, unless she is really that oblivious.  Her losing HP in order to play a mechanical golem is akin to her taking a piece of her own body and forming a mechanical golem out of it.

I kind of see her backstory as a little ambiguous as to her real nature. Maybe she IS Unity still, but everyone THINKS the real Unity is actually dead… kind of an existential question of what the self really is. 

I imagine it went down something like this: Unity received major injuries in battle and, say, lost her arm… so she replaced it with a mechanical arm. Later on she lost a leg and replaced it as well… then maybe part of her torso along with a lung or her liver and she replaced it… then part of head, ear, eye, portions of her brain stem.  All replaced. 

These parts became a part of her to the point where one day when her injuries were severe enough to make vital organs stop, like her heart… but her mechanical parts still had some juice stored and were still connected to her brain, so she was able to replace her vital organs as well, possibly after her teammates had pronounced her dead already. 

So in the end she might actually be the real and one and only Unity… it all depends on how you define your existence.  To her flesh-and-blood teammates, she died and this Golem Unity is but a copy. To her own consciousness, she is still the same since she never experienced a complete disruption in being. 

Thematically she can still use her powers and believe she is Unity, since as a technomancer she can use her own mechanical parts to build other golems. I also believe Inspired Repairs would be able help her regain some HP thematically in this situation since she'd simply be fixing her broken mechanical parts. 

I think I'm gonna house rule the Mechanical Golem type into her card and would actually like to see it placed there officially. I disagree that this would create any need to have to revise any existing hero character cards. Not all villains have a type on their character card, only the ones where this type can be affected by their deck.  It would be the same for heroes and right now this would only apply to Golem Unity's card. Tempest would have no need to mention his Maerynian-ness, nor Ra his godness, since there are no cards on their deck that affect those types. 

OK, that was a long rant.

If Unity is a Mechanical Golem that delusionally believes she is Unity, why would she come to any sane conclusion about herself?  Are we saying that insane beings should come to sane conclusions because it makes sense to?  We're playing (as presented in the write up) a Golem with delusions of humanity.  That isn't a bonus or a perk.  That is incredibly sad and a complete nightmare for someone or something to go through.  It's a severe limitation and the card's very damaging power and reduced HP represent that.  She doesn't get to be selectively sane, folks.  G-Unity is Unity as far as she is concerned, and she doesn't deal in mechanical prosthetics.  She's a Golem gal through and through.

I don't even know how the Energy damage she deals herself represents her process.  Maybe she spawns one from herself and rationalizes it like…I dunno…someone who is not all there?  Maybe she thinks she pulled a little mechanical bundle out of nowhere that cut her arm something good.  Maybe she thinks that the F.I.L.T.E.R. Agent that lives in her eye popped out and built the thing out of scraps of wood that spontaneously bubbled into metal and electricity.  I doubt that she would say "Oh wait…I'm obviously not Unity.  I'm an insane Golem-thing that has delusions of humanity.  Whelp, time to be an automaton wearing my former creator's face.  Yay!"

Or maybe she would…yikes!  But ask yourself this:  Does that make her any more inclined to accept her condition and make repairs on herself like she was a busted Construction Pylon on her Workbench?  And if she does, is she at that stage in the metaplot as presented?  From what I can tell from the Kickstarter, this is not the case.
